svg.title: Gold Stage A variable-weight calibration: composite risk under each winning weight set, both pin sets x both require_extras
svg.desc: IN-SAMPLE, AND THE OBJECTIVE IS A DIAGNOSTIC. Composite risk above is the shipped blend at each run's winning weights: a unitless 0..100 index, NOT a portfolio value, NOT an equity curve, NOT an allocation. Every indicator's params are a MAX over a frozen grid and every weight is a MAX over the weight grid, both scored against cycle windows derived from the SAME GLD history the series are built from, so these are partly-selected upper bounds, not out-of-sample evidence. The scored objective is cycle-window overlap, a shape diagnostic: THIS IS NOT A PERFORMANCE CLAIM AND NOT A BACKTEST RESULT. The published keep/drop is optimize_stage_a_by_backtest on in-sample vs_flat_dca_pct under a 10% deployed floor and a 50% drawdown cap; nothing here was kept or dropped on this figure. No return, Sharpe, drawdown, trade count or time-in-market is claimed. Stage A only: Stage B freezes weights, then regularize. Regenerate: digiquant/scripts/plot_gold_stage_a_weights.py
svg.text: Gold Stage A variable-weight calibration: composite risk under each winning weight set, both pin sets x both require_extras
four runs over GLD-USD 2004-11-18..2026-09-29 | accumulate band <= 35 / distribute band >= 80 | objective = spread + 25 x (trough_frac + peak_frac), a cycle-overlap SHAPE diagnostic
accumulate risk <= 35 (green rule) | distribute risk >= 80 (red rule) | objective = spread + 25 x (trough_frac + peak_frac)
trough window (green, buy side) and peak window (red, sell side) for that panel's pin set, ±45d; the dot on a panel's top edge marks the pin itself
20 turns from detect_turns at min_move_pct=15.0 (not individually listed; shaded on panels 3 and 4)
False may return valuation-only — reported, not buried. True forces at least one extra so a real blend has to win on the same objective. Both rows are shown for both pin sets.
the shipped blend's unitless 0..100 index (z clipped to [-3, 3]), NOT a portfolio value and NOT an equity curve
